extracted.intended_audience: early-career researchers (PIs) applying to the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program (pre-application and full application authors, and institutional research/administrative staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for preparing and submitting pre-applications and full applications to the DOE Office of Science Early Career Research Program, including eligibility, budget, submission format, review criteria, and award/administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'early career' (eligibility window)
rubrics_metrics.description: Principal Investigators are within 12 years of having received a Ph.D. (FY2023 competition extends window from 10 to 12 years). For this competition, doctorates received on or after January 1, 2010 are eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SC intends to continue the extended 12-year window for next year's competition then revert to 10 years later. Extensions considered for major life events (three months or longer absence).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible PI appointment types
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligible PIs are untenured assistant professors on the tenure track, untenured associate professors on the tenure track, or full-time, non-postdoctoral, permanent employees at a DOE national laboratory or an SC Scientific User Facility not at a DOE national laboratory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research professors and non-tenure-track appointments (even if titled Assistant Professor) are not eligible. You must be employed in the eligible position on the application due date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility extensions for major life events
rubrics_metrics.description: Extensions to eligibility will be considered for individuals who have had a major life event requiring an extended absence (three months or longer) from the workplace, including active military service, personal disability, or FMLA-covered absence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A letter signed by the dean, research vice president, or equivalent official stating the proposed PI will have no more than 12 years of full-time professional work experience as of the application deadline must be included with the pre-application. The letter must include NO personal information about the reason for the absence. The request will be evaluated as part of the pre-application assessment and determinations are not carried over between years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employment at application due date requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: You must be employed in the eligible position on the application due date (not merely hired/accepted if not yet receiving pay).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have only an offer or courtesy appointment but are not on payroll by the application due date, you are not eligible. If tenure is granted after the application due date but before an award is made, you remain eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: PI institutional/employment affiliation requirement (citizenship not required)
rubrics_metrics.description: The PI need not be a U.S. citizen, but must be employed by a U.S. academic institution, a DOE national laboratory, or an SC Scientific User Facility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work may be performed outside the U.S., but the application must be submitted through an eligible U.S. institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral fellows not eligible to apply directly
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral fellows may not apply directly as PIs to this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs may include postdoctoral support in the proposed budget, but postdocs cannot be the PI.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment-type eligibility determination procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine eligibility for appointment types not clearly permanent/postdoc, laboratory or SC User Facility director should answer five questions about the appointment type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five questions: (1) Is the appointment type considered to be a postdoctoral position? (2) Is an appointee an employee of the lab/SC User Facility? (3) Is the intention to transition appointees to career employment when appointments end? (4) Is the appointment full time? (5) Does the appointment qualify for full benefits? If question (1) is NO and all others are YES, the appointment type is eligible. Laboratories must follow DOE determinations; best practice is to clear ambiguous types with DOE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lists of previously approved/disapproved appointment types
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE provides charts of position types previously approved or disapproved for eligibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absence of a position type in the charts does not imply approval or disapproval. Limited term employees are not eligible unless specifically listed as eligible; if in doubt, email SC.Early@science.doe.gov.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional countersignature requirement for pre-applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-Applications must bear institutional countersignature and must be submitted by an authorized institutional representative (someone with 'Submit to DOE' privilege in PAMS).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PIs may draft pre-applications but cannot submit for institutional countersignature themselves. The acknowledgement email will go to the PI's email address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application is required and is selective (encourage/discourage)
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-application is required; pre-applications will be reviewed for responsiveness and competitiveness, and applicants will be encouraged or discouraged from submitting full applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applicants that receive an 'encouraged' notification may submit full applications. DOE will send encourage/discourage by email by the date on the FOA cover. Encouraged applicants are not required to submit the full application; discouraged pre-applications do not count as a participation attempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application review criteria (five criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: If topic receives many pre-applications, federal Program Managers may evaluate pre-applications on: (1) Responsiveness to the objectives of the FOA; (2) Scientific and technical merit; (3) Appropriateness of the proposed research approaches; (4) Likelihood of scientific impact; (5) Ensuring a diverse pool of applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-application comparative reviews compare pre-applications within topical fields with priority given to scientifically innovative and forward-looking basic research with the highest likelihood of success as a full application. Reviews are conducted by at least three federal program managers chosen for topical knowledge and diversity of perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application page limit and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre-applications must conform to the required format in the FOA and must not exceed three pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything submitted for the pre-application (including citations and figures) must fit within the three allowed pages. Minimum text font size: 11 point.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and citations in pre-application
rubrics_metrics.description: You may include figures in the three-page pre-application and may include citations, but all must fit within the three-page limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not exceed three pages under any circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: One pre-application per PI limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Only one pre-application may be submitted. If multiple are submitted, only the last one submitted will be reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit duplicate pre-applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application technical failure / late submission exception protocol
rubrics_metrics.description: If you could not submit pre-application due to PAMS technical issues, DOE will consider late submission only if you contacted PAMS help desk well before the deadline and can answer questions about timing and tracking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Email SC.Early@science.doe.gov with details and be prepared to provide help desk tracking number, call/email time, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full application submission method and deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Full applications must be submitted electronically through Grants.gov (FOA Number DE-FOA-0002821); the Grants.gov deadline is shown on the FOA cover. Late applications will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applicants that received DOE encouragement may submit full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: National laboratory full application submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: National Laboratories must submit full applications through Grants.gov and cannot submit full applications directly in PAMS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications must be submitted into PAMS, but full submissions for national labs go into Grants.gov. Check FOA for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not use Searchable FWP
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit proposals for this announcement into the Searchable FWP system; proposals submitted into Searchable FWP will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Laboratory proposals must be submitted into the DOE Office of Science PAMS website for pre-applications (and into Grants.gov for full applications as required).

rubrics_metrics.name: Field Work Proposal (FWP) not required at initial submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit or attach a DOE Field Work Proposal (FWP) at the time of application submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program office will request submission of FWPs later only from applicants selected for possible funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biosketch synergistic activities content (criterion 7 support)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of synergistic activities must be included in the biographical sketch (Appendix 1) describing professional and scholarly activities related to the proposed effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include information that helps reviewers evaluate your potential for leadership (criterion 7): invited/public lectures, awards, program committees, conference/workshop organization, society activities, partnerships, review/editorship duties, other leadership experiences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data management plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: A data management plan is required and must be included in Appendix 4 of the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the solicitation and DOE Office of Science Statement on Digital Data Management for guidance. Applications missing a data management plan will be declined without review. Budget may include data management costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promoting Inclusive and Equitable Research (PIER) plan required
rubrics_metrics.description: A PIER plan must be included in Appendix 5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the solicitation and the SC website guidance on PIER plans for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested reviewers / conflicts-of-interest handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not include a list of suggested reviewers NOT to involve inside the application; instead send such suggestions by email to the program manager (identify pre-application title and institution).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include this list in the application or pre-application because the application will be seen by reviewers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of recommendation not allowed
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of recommendation, endorsement, or support are not allowed in applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications that include recommendation letters will be subject to elimination from consideration during DOE’s initial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional letters of collaboration permitted with strict format
rubrics_metrics.description: Optional letters of collaboration may be included in Appendix 7 (Other Attachments), but each may contain two and only two sentences and must follow the provided template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template begins 'Dear <Principal Investigator Name>:' and must state intent to collaborate and a very short description of what the collaborator offers to do, followed by signature and name. These are not recommendation letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: No requirement for educational/outreach component
rubrics_metrics.description: An educational or outreach component is not required for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: No departmental letter required from academic PI
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic applicants are not required to include a letter from their department chair with the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cover page/header placement relative to page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Header information (institution, PI contact, FOA number, topic area, year doctorate awarded, etc.) may be placed on a separate cover page outside of the 15-page narrative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The narrative page limit is 15 pages (cover page does not count).

rubrics_metrics.name: PECASE eligibility and nomination criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: PECASE eligibility: as of closing date, a PI must be a U.S. citizen, national, or permanent resident and must not have previously received a PECASE. PECASE nominees are selected from PECASE-eligible winners of this program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PECASE review criteria: (1) pursuit of innovative research at the frontiers of science and technology; (2) commitment to community service demonstrated through scientific leadership, public education, or community outreach. DOE emphasizes scientific leadership for the second criterion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mailing address guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: List your professional or work mailing address (not your home address) on the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title/topic changes after pre-application
rubrics_metrics.description: Slight title changes are allowed, but the topical area may not change from the pre-application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your pre-application is encouraged by a particular program office, the application must be submitted to that program office and cannot be moved between program offices after submission. Pre-apps may be moved between topical areas by DOE prior to encouragement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Current and pending support: exclude startup funds
rubrics_metrics.description: The list of current and pending support should NOT include university startup funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format requirements located in FOA
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must conform to the format requirements in DE-FOA-0002821 (the FOA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the FOA at https://science.osti.gov/grants/FOAs/Open for full format details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviating long co-author lists in biosketch and bibliography
rubrics_metrics.description: You may abbreviate long co-author lists (e.g., 'A. Aardvark et al. (MONGO Collaboration)') to fit within page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using PRL convention (list only the first author followed by et al.) is allowed in publications list and bibliography.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table of contents allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: A table of contents is allowed in the proposal and will not count toward the 15-page narrative limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: No duplication of currently funded research
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposed research may not duplicate currently funded research (by DOE or other agencies); you must propose new research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may submit similar work to another agency (e.g., NSF CAREER), but you cannot be funded twice by the federal government for the same scope of work—if both fund you, you must accept only one award or ensure scope differs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-PI requirement (no co-PIs, no multi-PI large award)
rubrics_metrics.description: This is a single-Principal Investigator program. Co-Principal Investigators are not allowed and applications including co-PIs may be declined without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple early career investigators cannot be grouped into one large award; intention is to fund PI-directed and executed projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical area selection when idea spans areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Select a single topical area as the primary area for submission. If pre-application is encouraged by one program office, the full application must be submitted to that office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may contact the Technical Contact before pre-application if uncertain about fit. DOE may move pre-applications between topical areas before encouragement decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical support staff presence not required at submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical support staff (postdocs or students) do not need to be on board at the institution at the time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaboration with DOE national laboratory not required for academic applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Academic PIs are not required to collaborate with or make contact with a DOE national laboratory for a successful application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are judged on merit review criteria; collaboration with a lab is optional.

rubrics_metrics.name: No citizenship requirement for funded trainees
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students or postdocs supported by an award are not required to be U.S. citizens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-application required to submit full application (no back door)
rubrics_metrics.description: If you did not submit a pre-application, you may not submit a full application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only those who receive an encouragement email may submit full applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correcting errors before deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: To correct a typo before the deadline, resubmit the application through Grants.gov as a 'Changed/Corrected Application' and send email to SC.Early@science.doe.gov to notify DOE.

rubrics_metrics.name: No changes allowed after the deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to pre-applications or applications after the deadline are not allowed for any reason.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate full submissions handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If you submitted your application through Grants.gov twice, notify SC.Early@science.doe.gov if you have a preference; otherwise DOE will consider the application that arrived last and disregard the earlier one.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when pre-application transferred to different Program Manager
rubrics_metrics.description: If DOE transfers your pre-application to a different Program Manager, indicate the new topic area and program manager’s name on the cover page of the full application; contact SC.Early@science.doe.gov if the new PM is not listed in the solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical encouragement rate and potential for programmatic discouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: Historically, about 80% of pre-applications have been encouraged, but if a topic receives a large number of pre-applications, Program Managers may discourage more to reduce low-probability full submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discouraging intends to avoid applicants spending resources preparing unlikely-to-succeed full applications, and to prevent discouraged pre-applications from counting against PI submission limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer review format and alignment with review criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications may be reviewed by mail review, panel review, or a combination; each program decides its review method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare the proposed research to be responsive to the review criteria and the Office of Science mission areas and follow the required format to be ready for any review process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer scoring and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide narrative comments for each of the seven merit review criteria and an overall integer numerical rating between 1 and 6: Strongly Encourage Funding (5 or 6); Encourage Funding (3 or 4); Discourage Funding (1 or 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative comments accompany each criterion; reviewers provide an overall rating for the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection official's considerations beyond reviewer scores
rubrics_metrics.description: Not all applications above a certain score will automatically be funded. The Selection Official will consider merit review scores, written recommendations, program policy factors, and available funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program policy factors may include alignment with existing/planned projects, utilization of existing/planned facilities, promoting diversity of supported investigators and institutions, and increasing participation of historically underrepresented institutions in the SC portfolio.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidance on evaluating Criterion 7 (Potential for Leadership)
rubrics_metrics.description: Criterion 7 should be interpreted broadly; reviewers should identify researchers early in careers who can develop new scientific ideas, promote them, and convince peers to pursue them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appendix 1 provides information to evaluate leadership (invited talks, awards, program committee service, conference organization, society activities, partnerships, review/editorship duties). Use professional judgment of what scientific leadership means. Criterion 7 input is used for PECASE nomination decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award duration and tenure status
rubrics_metrics.description: An award is for five years, and receiving tenure after an award is granted does not force you to give up the award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards continue assuming satisfactory progress and available funds. If PI changes appointment type that conflicts with eligibility (e.g., leaves full-time lab position), transfer rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Laboratory/SC User Facility award minimums and PI salary charging requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum award size is approximately $875,000 for five years for universities and approximately $2,500,000 for five years for national laboratories or SC User Facilities. Laboratory/SC User Facility awards must cover at least 50% of the PI salary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically average academic award ~$750,000 over five years (~$150k/year); typical lab awards ~$500k/year. Requests larger than averages/floors require sufficient justification. Minimums include indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget minimum includes indirect costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The minimum budget specified includes both direct and indirect costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: No cost sharing required
rubrics_metrics.description: This program does not require cost sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget distribution flexibility (but lab salary rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: You may distribute the cumulative minimum budget across the five award years as you wish, but the five-year total should approximate the minimum; labs must charge at least 50% of PI salary to the award each year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAMS allows a maximum of five budget periods and entries must be one-year increments (do not enter six FY-based budget periods).

rubrics_metrics.name: PAMS budget period constraints
rubrics_metrics.description: PAMS allows a maximum of five budget periods and budgets should be completed in one-year increments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your institution's tools prefer six fiscal-year entries, you must still enter five one-year increments in PAMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Co-PI prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: There may not be a co-Principal Investigator on an application; applications including co-PIs may be declined without review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paid collaborator policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Paid collaborators are generally discouraged; the intention is to fund PI-directed and executed projects, but in rare cases a paid collaborator (early career or senior) bringing something unique may be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preference is that the project be PI-led with research support staff (students, postdocs), travel, supplies, equipment, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable budget items
rubrics_metrics.description: Budget may include equipment, travel, graduate students, other participants, and data management costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Encouraged pre-application must remain in same program office
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a pre-application is encouraged by a particular program office, the full application must be submitted to and reviewed within that same office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is important because offices may have additional data management or other requirements; applications will not be moved between program offices after arrival.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award transfer rules when PI changes appointment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a lab or SC user facility scientist who has an award accepts a 50/50 joint position with a university, they cannot keep the award at the lab because they would no longer be full-time at the lab. To transfer award to a university, the PI must move into a tenure-track or tenured position and the new institution must submit an application under transfer rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there is no change in scope, work can be transferred; if scope changes, DOE will review and decide. Award amount may be reduced appropriately when transferring from lab to university.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested award start date
rubrics_metrics.description: Suggested reasonable start date for award is July 1, 2023.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAMS registration and help
rubrics_metrics.description: PAMS registration is a two-step process: create an individual account and then associate with ('register to') your institution. For help, use the External User Guide or contact the PAMS Help Desk (phone and email provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pre-applications must be submitted directly into PAMS; PAMS is integrated with Grants.gov so grant applications submitted into Grants.gov are imported into and stored by PAMS.
